paragraphs: R. Chanina ben Gamliel of Yavneh.

(a) In the Mishnah: Kiddushin 3:4; Bava Batra 10:1; Makkot 3:15; Menachot 5:8, where the name is Chananyah. Bekhorot 6:9, 40b, and Nedarim 62a have Chananyah; so too Tosefta Kilayim 5:13 [received end of chapter 4]. End of Moed Katan, 23a: Chananyah ben Gamliel would say a legal teaching and aggadah in a mourner's house. In the Tosefta, Berakhot chapter 3, 22a, and Avodah Zarah 34b, 39b, R. Yehudah ben Gamliel speaks in R. Chanina ben Gamliel's name. Jerusalem Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, has R. Chanina ben Gamliel in R. Yehudah ben Gamliel's name. Apparently he was his brother. He was a great scholar.

(b) Sifra, Emor, and Tosefta Yoma, chapter 1: Pinchas of the Birah was chosen by lot to be high priest. They found him quarrying stones and filled the quarry with gold dinars. R. Chanina ben Gamliel said, “Was he a stonecutter? Was he not our son-in-law, etc.?” On this basis it appears he lived in the Temple period and lived long, since he was also in R. Shimon's and R. Meir's time. This is impossible: Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh was young at the destruction (see there); how could his son's son-in-law have been high priest while the Temple stood? But I found in Tosafot, Niddah, chapter 1, 8b: how did he say “our son-in-law”? If this was R. Chanina ben Gamliel of Yavneh, how could he have a high-priest son-in-law? He lived after the destruction. One may answer that he did not literally mean “our son-in-law,” but an ancestor's son-in-law. This is indicated by his saying “our son-in-law,” rather than “my son-in-law.” End of quotation. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 32a, says he was the brother of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, Rabbi's father; R. Chanina ben Gamliel was Rabbi's uncle. In the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon in Yuchasin, R. Chanina ben Gamliel and R. Yehudah ben Gamliel are placed in the time of R. Yishmael son of R. Yochanan ben Beroka and R. Yehoshua ben Korcha. Chelek, 111a, near the end, has R. Chanina ben Gamla, but Ein Yaakov has ben Gamliel. He is also credited with saying, “R. Meir’s words appear correct.” See R. Chanina ben Antigonos above.

(c) Gittin, chapter 1, 7a: he imposed excessive fear in his household, and his servants sought to feed him a limb from a living animal. Gilgulei Neshamot, letter pe, subentry 10 [source ג״נ], writes: he was a repair of the man of the concubine, who imposed excessive fear on his wife, as stated there. He came to repair his former deeds, when he had imposed excessive fear, but now stumbled a second time. He recognized the matter, took care, and did not eat. End of quotation.

(d) R. Abba spoke in his name: Nedarim 53a. R. Abbahu, in his name: Avodah Zarah 39b; Kiddushin 81b; Nedarim 62a. R. Gamliel son of R. Chanina—perhaps his son. R. Chananyah ben Akashya; see there. He disagrees in the Mishnah with R. Yosi HaGelili. R. Yosi son of R. Chanina, in his name. R. Yosi said, “These are R. Chanina ben Gamliel's words”: Tosefta Negaim, chapter 2. R. Yitzchak bar Nachman, in his name. R. Krispa, in his name. R. Shimon said, “I found Chanina ben Gamliel, and he told me, ‘A cow, etc.’ I said to him, etc.” They said to him, “But in your name they told R. Elazar”: Tosefta Parah 4:5 [received chapter 3].
